title: US-Canada Trade Conflict Deepens as New Tariffs Announced
subtitle: President Trump plans to increase taxes on Canadian cars and steel as both nations trade blame over failed negotiations.

summary.en: The trade relationship between the United States and Canada has worsened significantly this week. President Donald Trump announced that tariffs on Canadian automobiles and steel will rise to 50% on January 1. This follows the collapse of trade talks last weekend. Canada has promised to respond with its own taxes on American goods. Both nations are now preparing for a long and difficult economic standoff.
summary.zh: 美國與加拿大之間的貿易關係本週顯著惡化。川普總統宣布，自一月一日起，針對加拿大汽車與鋼鐵的關稅將提高至百分之五十。此舉發生在上週末貿易談判破裂之後。加拿大已承諾將對美國商品徵收報復性關稅。兩國目前正為一場長期且艱難的經濟對峙做準備。

paragraphs.en: The trade conflict between the United States and Canada reached a new level of intensity this week. On Monday, US President Donald Trump announced that he will increase tariffs — taxes on imported goods — on Canadian automobiles, trucks, and steel. Starting January 1, 2027, these goods will face a 50% tax. This move is a major escalation in a dispute that has already seen both countries impose new costs on each other’s products.
paragraphs.zh: 美國與加拿大之間的貿易衝突在本週升溫至新的層級。週一，美國總統川普宣布，將提高針對加拿大汽車、卡車與鋼鐵的關稅（即進口商品稅）。自二〇二七年一月一日起，這些商品將面臨百分之五十的稅率。此舉標誌著這場爭端出現重大升級，此前兩國已針對彼此的產品施加了新的成本負擔。

paragraphs.en: This announcement follows the collapse of trade negotiations late last week. According to BBC Business, the talks failed after both sides accused the other of making unreasonable demands at the last minute. The US had already imposed a 50% tax on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, including electronics and sports equipment, which took effect over the weekend. US trade representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC that the US felt forced to act to protect American workers and supply chains after a year of what he called retaliation from its neighbor.
paragraphs.zh: 這項宣布是在上週末貿易談判破裂後發出的。根據英國廣播公司商業頻道（BBC Business）報導，談判失敗的原因是雙方皆指責對方在最後一刻提出不合理的要求。美國此前已對價值約兩百億美元的加拿大商品（包括電子產品與運動器材）徵收百分之五十的稅，並於週末生效。美國貿易代表傑米森·格里爾（Jamieson Greer）向美國消費者新聞與商業頻道（CNBC）表示，在經歷了一年所謂來自鄰國的報復後，美國認為必須採取行動以保護美國勞工與供應鏈。

paragraphs.en: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has strongly criticized the American position. Speaking from Quebec, Carney described the US actions as an attempt to use economic integration as a weapon. He stated that Canada is ready to return to the negotiating table, but only if the US approaches the talks with a “true partnership” and the “right attitude.” According to The Guardian, Carney also warned that these policies will hurt workers in American states like Michigan and Ohio, which rely heavily on Canadian demand for their products.
paragraphs.zh: 加拿大總理馬克·卡尼（Mark Carney）強烈批評美國的立場。卡尼在魁北克發表談話時，形容美國的行為是試圖將經濟整合當作武器。他表示，加拿大準備好重返談判桌，但前提是美國必須以「真正的夥伴關係」與「正確的態度」進行對話。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，卡尼也警告，這些政策將傷害密西根州與俄亥俄州等美國州的勞工，因為這些州高度依賴加拿大對其產品的需求。

paragraphs.en: As the situation worsens, both sides have begun to prepare for a long economic fight. Prime Minister Carney announced that Canada will respond with “dollar-for-dollar” retaliatory tariffs. These taxes, which are expected to begin on September 8, will target a wide range of American goods, including steel, dairy products, and agricultural equipment. Additionally, the Canadian government is looking for ways to support its businesses and reduce its historical reliance on the US market. This includes a new C$11 billion investment to build six icebreakers, which will help improve shipping routes through northern and Atlantic waters.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著局勢惡化，雙方皆已開始為長期的經濟戰做準備。卡尼總理宣布，加拿大將採取「等值」的報復性關稅作為回應。這些預計於九月八日生效的稅項，將針對廣泛的美國商品，包括鋼鐵、乳製品與農業設備。此外，加拿大政府正尋求各種方式來支持國內企業，並減少對美國市場長久以來的依賴。這包括一項總額一百一十億加幣的投資計畫，用於建造六艘破冰船，以協助改善通過北部與大西洋水域的航運路線。

paragraphs.en: The tone between the two leaders has become increasingly sharp. President Trump has used social media to express his frustration, claiming that Canada has been “ripping off” the US for years. He stated that the US no longer needs to treat Canada like a partner, writing that Canada needs the US more than the US needs Canada. Meanwhile, Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who leads the province where most of Canada’s auto industry is located, responded with very angry language toward the US president. Trump later criticized Ford in a social media post, warning that the consequences for Canada could become much worse if the country does not “fall in line.”
paragraphs.zh: 兩國領導人之間的語氣變得愈發尖銳。川普總統利用社群媒體表達不滿，聲稱加拿大多年來一直在「敲詐」美國。他表示，美國不再需要將加拿大視為夥伴，並寫道加拿大對美國的需求遠大於美國對加拿大的需求。與此同時，加拿大汽車工業重鎮安大略省的省長道格·福特（Doug Ford）以極為憤怒的言詞回應美國總統。川普隨後在社群媒體貼文中批評福特，警告若加拿大不「乖乖配合」，後果可能會變得更嚴重。

paragraphs.en: The impact of this trade war is expected to be widespread. Canada is a major supplier of energy to the US, providing roughly 60% of its crude oil imports and almost all of its natural gas. Experts and business leaders are concerned that the ongoing tension will disrupt these vital supply chains. According to Deutsche Welle, the US currently accounts for about 70% of all Canadian exports, which makes Canada more vulnerable to these changes. With no further negotiations currently scheduled, it is unclear how or when this conflict will end.
paragraphs.zh: 這場貿易戰的影響預計將十分廣泛。加拿大是美國主要的能源供應國，提供約百分之六十的進口原油與幾乎所有的天然氣。專家與企業領袖擔心，持續的緊張局勢將擾亂這些至關重要的供應鏈。根據德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導，美國目前佔加拿大出口總額的百分之七十左右，這使得加拿大在這些變動中更顯脆弱。由於目前沒有安排進一步的談判，這場衝突將如何或何時結束仍不明朗。

paragraphs.en: For now, the two countries remain at a standstill. The collapse of the recent talks marks a major change from just a week ago, when officials from both sides seemed hopeful that a new deal could be reached. Instead, the focus has shifted to how each country will manage the economic damage caused by these new taxes. As the deadline for the higher auto tariffs approaches in January, businesses on both sides of the border are watching closely to see if there is any chance for a peaceful resolution.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，兩國仍處於僵局。近期談判的破裂與一週前的情況形成鮮明對比，當時雙方官員似乎都對達成新協議抱持希望。如今，焦點已轉向兩國將如何應對這些新稅項所造成的經濟損害。隨著一月份汽車關稅提高的期限逼近，邊境兩側的企業正密切關注，看是否還有任何和平解決的機會。

quiz.question: What specific action did the US government take that will take effect on January 1, 2027?

options.A: A 50% tax on all Canadian energy imports like oil and natural gas.
options.B: A 50% tax on Canadian automobiles, trucks, and steel products.
options.C: A retaliatory tax on Canadian dairy and agricultural equipment.
options.D: A total ban on the import of all goods from the province of Ontario.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據文章第一段，美國總統宣布將針對加拿大的汽車、卡車和鋼鐵產品徵收 50% 的關稅，且生效日期為 2027 年 1 月 1 日。選項 A 錯誤，因為能源進口目前未列入此關稅清單；選項 C 的農產品與乳製品關稅是加拿大針對美國的反制措施，而非美國的行動；選項 D 則完全未在文中提及。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might the US trade conflict with Canada lead to economic difficulties for specific American states?

options.A: Because American states are forced to pay for the construction of Canadian icebreakers.
options.B: Because the US government plans to stop all exports of electronics to Canada.
options.C: Because some American states rely on Canadian demand for their own locally produced goods.
options.D: Because the US government has decided to prioritize trade with other countries over Canada.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據文章第三段，加拿大總理 Carney 指出這些貿易政策會傷害美國密西根州與俄亥俄州的工人，因為這些州非常依賴加拿大對其產品的需求。這暗示了貿易戰是雙向的，會造成經濟連鎖反應。選項 A 文中未提；選項 B 與貿易戰的起因不符；選項 D 則是過度推論，文章並未提及美國轉向其他貿易夥伴。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the phrase 'fall in line' mean in the context of President Trump's comment to Premier Doug Ford?

options.A: To agree with and follow the instructions of someone in power.
options.B: To stand in a straight row during a formal meeting.
options.C: To decrease the amount of taxes being collected.
options.D: To physically move across the border into the United States.

quiz.explanationZh: 在文中，川普總統警告如果加拿大不「fall in line」，後果會更嚴重。這裡的片語意指「順從」或「配合」，即要求對方服從自己的立場。選項 B 是字面意義的誤解；選項 C 與關稅增加的語境相反；選項 D 則與地理移動無關，完全偏離文意。

options.A: The trade war is primarily a personal conflict between President Trump and Premier Doug Ford.

options.C: The trade relationship between the US and Canada has deteriorated, leading to mutual economic damage and uncertainty.
options.D: The two countries are expected to reach a peaceful resolution before the end of the year.

quiz.explanationZh: 全文主要探討美加貿易衝突的升級，包括關稅報復、談判破裂以及對雙方經濟造成的潛在損害與不確定性。選項 A 僅是衝突的一小部分；選項 B 過於樂觀，文中僅提到加拿大試圖減少依賴；選項 D 與文章最後一段提到「不確定衝突如何結束」的論點完全相反。
